criteriaApplied: C4 Regular Audit (documentation/Severity-criteria.md): High = direct asset theft/loss with no hypotheticals; Medium = protocol function/availability impacted or value leak with stated assumptions; Low/QA = state handling, spec deviations, defensive hardening, dust losses, gas-only losses.

findings.title: BatchNFTMinter wired to V1 ITokenMinter interface; non-functional against production NFTMinterV2

classification.assetImpact: No assets at risk. Every batchMint reverts atomically on the first inner mint() call (selector miss against V2). The safeTransferFrom from msg.sender is undone in the same revert. User loses gas only; no funds can be stuck or stolen.
attackPath: User calls BatchNFTMinter.batchMint(nftMinter=NFTMinterV2, ...)
Helper executes safeTransferFrom(msg.sender -> contract, paymentAmount)
Helper executes forceApprove(nftMinter, type(uint256).max)
First loop iteration calls nftMinter.mint(address,uint256,address) — selector 0xff.. does not exist on V2 (V2 only has mint(uint256,address) and mint(uint256,address,bytes))
Call reverts; entire transaction reverts; safeTransferFrom and forceApprove are rolled back
User loses gas; no batch mint ever succeeds
classification.likelihood: Certain — every invocation against the production V2 minter reverts deterministically.
classification.assumptions: Production wiring is NFTMinterV2 (verified by INFTSupply.sol natspec L15-L18 — direct cast of deployed NFTMinterV2 address).

findings.severityRationale: DOWNGRADED from high to medium. C4 High requires assets to be 'stolen/lost/compromised'. Here no funds are at risk: atomic revert returns the user's prepayment in the same tx. The impact is a complete denial-of-service of a deployed user-facing helper contract (BatchNFTMinter is the recommended batch-mint entrypoint per its NatSpec and was added in story-009 as a UX optimisation). C4 Medium covers 'function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted' — a deployed helper that is 100% non-functional against the spec-bound production minter is the textbook example. Not invalid: the contract is deployed and is part of the product surface, not dead code; users will reasonably try to use it. Not High: the loss is gas + foregone optimisation, never principal. The defect is deterministic and trivial to demonstrate, supporting a confident Medium.

findings.title: batchMint has no per-mint or cumulative price ceiling; front-runner can bump price between submission and inclusion, gas-griefing the entire batch

classification.assetImpact: Caller loses tx gas only. Atomic rollback (documented in NatSpec L26-L27) means the dispatcher cannot pull more than the prepaid paymentAmount: if cumulative cost exceeds it, an inner mint reverts and the entire batch unwinds, returning the prepayment to the caller. No principal loss path.
attackPath: Honest user submits batchMint(count=N, paymentAmount=P) sized for current dispatcher price
Front-runner observes the tx in the mempool and inserts their own mint() before it
Dispatcher price compounds by (1+g/10000); honest user's cumulative cost now exceeds P
Honest user's tx reverts atomically; user pays only gas
Front-runner secured the cheaper slot; honest user must retry with a larger budget
classification.likelihood: Plausible on any non-private mempool. Bot competition for the early-minter geometric APY premium is a known incentive on this protocol.
classification.assumptions: Public mempool. growthBasisPoints > 0 (otherwise no per-mint price growth and no griefing surface).

findings.severityRationale: DOWNGRADED from medium to low. C4 treats pure gas-only losses (where principal is fully refunded by atomic rollback) as Low/QA. The recommendation (add a maxStartingPrice / maxCumulativePrice param) is a quality-of-service hardening, not a fix for a value-loss bug. Distinct from a sandwich that actually steals funds — here the protocol's atomic rollback already prevents overpayment. Recommendation goes into the QA report.

findings.title: batchMint forfeits dispatcher-side slippage protection by passing empty extraData on every iteration

classification.assetImpact: Caller's prepaid paymentAmount is exposed to MEV sandwich attacks on the Balancer pool leg. Unlike DEDUP-002 (gas-only via atomic revert), here the dispatcher can succeed at a worse pool execution price — the mint completes, but a larger fraction of paymentAmount is consumed per mint than the user expected at submission time. The single-mint extraData overload exists precisely to bound this; batch callers cannot reach it.
attackPath: Honest user calls batchMint(count=N, paymentAmount=P) intending to receive N NFTs at the current pool-quoted cost
MEV searcher front-runs with a Balancer swap that moves the pool against the user's payment direction
Inside each loop iteration, BalancerPoolerV2 dispatcher swaps the user's payment-token at the now-degraded pool quote (no slippage params to revert with)
Each mint succeeds at a higher effective price; cumulative cost approaches paymentAmount — user receives N NFTs but pays substantially more than the spot-quoted price would have implied
Searcher back-runs to capture the pool imbalance
classification.likelihood: Plausible on any large batch; price-impact-driven loss scales with count and pool depth.
classification.assumptions: Underlying dispatcher (BalancerPoolerV2 today) routes payment through a Balancer pool. The single-mint overload supports slippage params; batch callers are denied feature parity.
classification.externalRequirements: Public mempool with MEV. Dispatcher exposes a slippage-aware overload that batch path does not propagate to.

findings.severityRationale: KEEP at medium. C4 Medium fits: 'Assets not at direct risk, but the function of the protocol... could be impacted, or leak value with a hypothetical attack path with stated assumptions, but external requirements.' The assumption (Balancer-pool-routing dispatcher) and external requirement (MEV-active mempool) are both satisfied by current production wiring. Distinct from DEDUP-002: here actual paymentAmount is consumed at worse-than-quoted prices (atomic-rollback does NOT save the user because the swap simply succeeds at a degraded rate), so the loss is real value extraction not just gas. Note: this finding is conditioned on DEDUP-001 being fixed (V2 retargeting) — once retargeted, the V2 mint(uint256,address,bytes) overload still needs to be used, and the same mitigation framing applies.

findings.title: batchMint pre-approves nftMinter for type(uint256).max for the entire loop, exposing the full paymentAmount to the configured dispatcher

classification.assetImpact: Latent. Allowance is set to 0 immediately after the loop (line 76 forceApprove(nftMinter, 0)) so no residual approval survives the call. During the loop the dispatcher could in principle pull the full paymentAmount in one go rather than the metered per-mint price. Today's BalancerPoolerV2 dispatcher does not exhibit this behavior; the surface is a defensive hardening recommendation rather than an exploitable bug.
attackPath: [Hypothetical] An owner registers a hostile dispatcher OR an existing dispatcher gains a callback path
Inside the loop, the dispatcher pulls the full type(uint256).max approval (capped by contract balance == paymentAmount) instead of just the metered per-mint price
Dispatcher returns success; subsequent mint iterations still succeed (or revert harmlessly); contract is drained of its prepayment with fewer than N NFTs delivered
classification.likelihood: Low. Requires either (a) an owner-introduced hostile dispatcher (centralization assumption already covered by yield-claim-nft known issues) or (b) a future callback bug in a benign dispatcher.
classification.assumptions: Dispatcher trust model. The stated trust assumption in yield-claim-nft is that dispatchers are owner-vetted; this finding amplifies that surface for batch callers (full prepaid balance vs per-mint metered amount).
classification.externalRequirements: Hostile or buggy dispatcher; not currently the case.

findings.severityRationale: CONFIRM low. The cleanup forceApprove(0) on line 76 means no allowance survives the call, which substantially limits the surface. The remaining concern is intra-call dispatcher trust amplification — defensive hardening at best. Goes into the QA report with a one-line forceApprove(paymentAmount) recommendation.

findings.title: BatchNFTMinter collapses multi-tx mint cadence into a single transaction, simultaneously amplifying L-04 runway depletion and concentrating the early-minter geometric APY premium

classification.assetImpact: No principal loss path. The geometric APY premium ('earlier minters earn targetAPY * r^k') is documented intentional behavior (registered-projects.json L514, phoenix-nft-staking-05 M-03-submission L130). Honest later stakers still earn the advertised targetAPY floor. The 'loss' is opportunity cost relative to a hypothetical even arrival distribution that the spec never committed to. The L-04 runway-acceleration angle is a re-statement of a prior-audit Low.
attackPath: First user to interact with the freshly-deployed dispatcher calls batchMint(count=N) atomically
Dispatcher price compounds N times; first user captures r^N + r^(N-1) + ... + r^1 share of the early-minter premium pool in one tx
Subsequent organic minters pay higher latestPrice and earn exactly targetAPY (not the multiple)
[L-04 amplification] NFTStaker._recomputeSchedule next-fired sees a sharply higher latestPrice => higher rewardRate => shorter runway
classification.likelihood: Plausible for any first-mover with capital. The behavior is permissionless-by-design.
classification.assumptions: growthBasisPoints > 0 (otherwise no premium chain). The spec documents APY-as-floor, not APY-as-fair-distribution.

findings.severityRationale: DOWNGRADED from medium to low. The bulk of the framing restates documented intentional behavior (geometric APY-as-floor). The novel single-tx-capture angle does not cause value loss to honest stakers — they still receive their advertised targetAPY floor; what changes is the upper-bound earned by the first-mover, which is a design-disclosed parameter. The L-04 amplification angle is genuinely additive (the prior Low was framed as multi-tx; batching collapses this to one tx) but the underlying mechanism (runway shortens with latestPrice growth) is already an acknowledged Low. Operator-side runway-management documentation update belongs in the QA report. Not Medium because no honest-staker value leak materially exceeds what the spec already disclosed; not invalid because the L-04 amplification via a new code path is a legitimate re-flag.

findings.title: M-03 staked-subset notional S = totalStaked * latestPrice uses bare multiplication; safe for documented param envelope but unprotected against future high-supply / high-price configs

classification.assetImpact: No exploitable loss today. If parameters drift outside the documented envelope (totalStaked * latestPrice approaching 2^256), Solidity 0.8 checked arithmetic reverts in _recomputeSchedule, DoS-ing every user-facing function except emergencyWithdraw. Solvency is preserved (principal recoverable via emergencyWithdraw).
attackPath: [Hypothetical] Owner reconfigures dispatcher to a higher-supply token ID + sustained mints push latestPrice into the high range
totalStaked * latestPrice overflows uint256 in _recomputeSchedule
stake / unstake / claim / topUp / setTargetAPY / setDispatcherIndex / setNFTMinter / pullAndRefresh all revert
Stakers exit via emergencyWithdraw (forfeiting pending reward)
classification.likelihood: Low. Requires parameter drift outside the natspec-documented envelope.
classification.assumptions: Future configuration changes that exceed the documented bounds.
classification.externalRequirements: Owner action that changes stakedId or growthBasisPoints to push the product past 2^256.

findings.severityRationale: CONFIRM low. Defensive hardening recommendation. Documented parameter envelope keeps the product well below 2^256; the suggested mulDiv / explicit overflow-precheck makes the contract robust to future configuration changes. Solvency invariant preserved via emergencyWithdraw escape hatch. QA report.

findings.title: totalPaid return value reports 0 when caller actually spent paymentAmount and received an unrelated donation refund as a windfall

classification.assetImpact: No on-chain asset loss. The caller's wallet flow is internally consistent: paid the dispatcher the real cost, received a donor-funded refund as a windfall, net wallet position correct. Only the helper's totalPaid return value is wrong — an off-chain accounting/integrator gotcha.
attackPath: Third party donates D wei of paymentToken to BatchNFTMinter (windfall, no malicious intent required)
Caller invokes batchMint(paymentAmount=P) which costs C < P + D
Loop completes; remaining = P + D - C
Sweep transfers (P + D - C) back to caller; clamp returns totalPaid = P > remaining ? P - remaining : 0
If P + D - C > P (i.e. D > C), totalPaid = 0 even though the dispatcher charged C of real cost
Off-chain integrator records the mint as zero-cost
classification.likelihood: Low. Requires a non-trivial donation. Documented donation-flow-forward behavior makes this a corner case rather than a likely production scenario.
classification.assumptions: Donations occur (per NatSpec, this is acknowledged as possible).
classification.externalRequirements: Off-chain consumer that trusts the totalPaid return value.

findings.severityRationale: CONFIRM low. Off-chain accounting gotcha with no on-chain asset risk. Either snapshot pre-call balance (computing totalPaid against the actual contract delta) or document the asymmetry in NatSpec. QA report.

reclassifications.reason: Atomic revert means user loses only gas, not principal. C4 High requires asset theft/loss; protocol-function denial of a deployed helper fits Medium.
Atomic rollback prevents overpayment; loss is gas-only. C4 treats gas-only losses as Low/QA.

Bulk of framing restates documented intentional APY-as-floor behavior. Novel single-tx-capture angle does not cause honest-staker value leak. L-04 amplification via new code path is a legitimate Low re-flag.
